work.genre: Народная литературная сказка в редакции братьев Гримм
work.informant: No individual oral informant is named in the consulted 1819 source; the tale is presented as a traditional folk narrative collected and edited by the Brothers Grimm.
work.edition: Kinder- und Haus-Märchen, second edition, volume 1, KHM 27, printed pages 141–145
work.publication_status: Published during the lifetimes of both named editors; not anonymous, pseudonymous, or first published posthumously.

source_materials.exact_basis: Public domain; economic copyright term has expired.
source_materials.source_quality: The Wikisource page identifies the 1819 edition and states that the text was proofread twice against the source. The five original page scans were checked individually; each Commons file page marks the scan Public Domain and links to the Creative Commons Public Domain Mark 1.0.
source_materials.commercial_use_reason: The underlying text was published in 1819 under the names of the Brothers Grimm, while both were alive. It is not a posthumous or anonymous work. The last surviving co-editor died in 1863. The original text is reproduced here only as the basis for a new Russian translation; the old scan images are not embedded in BookCheef.
source_materials.attribution: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, Die Bremer Stadtmusikanten (KHM 27), 1819 edition, volume 1, pages 141–145. Digital source transcription: German Wikisource. Original page scans: Wikimedia Commons, files 141–145, Public Domain Mark 1.0.
source_materials.changes: Translated anew into Russian; no modern third-party translation, modern commentary, or modern illustration was used.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Directive 2006/116/EC, Article 1: life of the author plus 70 years; for joint works, the term is measured from the death of the last surviving author.
jurisdiction_review.application: Last surviving co-editor Jacob Grimm died in 1863. The term ended on 31 December 1933; the work has been in the public domain since 1 January 1934.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Urheberrechtsgesetz §§64–65 and §69: 70 years after the author or last surviving joint author; calculation begins at the end of the calendar year.
jurisdiction_review.application: The 1819 work is public domain since 1 January 1934. It was published during the editors' lifetimes, so the special right for a first posthumous publication does not apply.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Government guidance: copyright expires 70 years after the creator's death, counted from 1 January of the following year.
jurisdiction_review.application: Last surviving co-editor died in 1863; the economic term expired long ago.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Copyright and Related Rights Act, consolidated text Dz.U. 2025 poz. 24, Article 36 (joint works: death of the last surviving co-author) and Article 39 (full years after the triggering year). Article 40 is repealed in the consolidated text.
jurisdiction_review.application: Last surviving co-editor died in 1863; the economic term expired on 31 December 1933. The current consolidated act confirms Article 40 is repealed.

jurisdiction_review.basis: Federal Law on Copyright, WIPO Lex, current 2026 version, Article 29: life plus 100 years; for co-authors, counted from the death of the last co-author.
jurisdiction_review.application: Even under this longer 100-year term, the work entered the public domain no later than 1 January 1964.

jurisdiction_review.basis: The original edition was published in 1819, before 1 January 1931; the Commons file pages also identify the historical scans as public domain in the United States.
jurisdiction_review.application: The original text and the 1819 scans are public domain in the United States.
